fields.name: Requests
fields.evidence: Creator bg3.exe+0x34FF0B0 allocates 0x10 bytes; destructor bg3.exe+0x22CF870 -> bg3.exe+0x22E29E0 destroys elements with stride 0xE0 (variant destructor bg3.exe+0x22D5900 at element + 0x10) and frees the buffer. In bg3.exe+0x3473C80 (esv::inventory::InteractionRequestSystem, registration bg3.exe+0x2375A40, callback bg3.exe+0x239C720) the singleton (stride 0x10) is passed, when its size at +0x0C is non-zero, to bg3.exe+0x3474D70 - the very function that is then called for the system's own array at system + 0x20, which Script Extender declares as InteractionRequestSystem::MemberInteraction = Array<MemberInteractionRequestData> (Components/Inventory.h); that array is cleared with the same bg3.exe+0x22E29E0 and the same 0xE0 stride. So the element type is the existing esv::inventory::MemberInteractionRequestData (reuse, do not redeclare). Written by esv::inventory::EquipmentSystem (registration bg3.exe+0x2378C70 lists the component in its first, written, set). Probe: null/empty.

open_questions: sizeof(MemberInteractionRequestData) in Script Extender should come out as 0xE0 (EntityHandle, int Amount, variant whose largest member is MemberDropData); worth a static_assert when the component is added.
Which variant alternatives EquipmentSystem actually queues (probably MemberAddData / MemberEquipmentRequestFailedData) was not checked.
